passages.title: The thin margin
paragraphs: City governments now compete for skilled workers who can live almost anywhere. A new campus or a tax cut is often alleged to accelerate growth. The estimates, however, rarely survive contact with the housing market.

Where the margin between wages and rent is already thin, a severe shortage of small flats matters more than another slogan. Officials are prone to treat a press release as a policy. An effective initiative is usually dull: it suspends a rule that blocks small homes, then checks whether builders actually show up.

Optimistic forecasts still transform the headlines. They seldom transform a lease. Cities that prevail are the ones that can indicate, in numbers rather than adjectives, that an ordinary household can remain.

quiz.q: The author suggests that official growth estimates
options: are usually confirmed by the housing market
often fail once rent is taken into account
depend on a new campus being built
have already solved the shortage of flats
quiz.why: however 后面才是观点：估计一碰到房租就站不住。A 把转折说反了。

passages.title: After the dry year
paragraphs: A long drought does more than fill the news. It cuts acreage and leaves farmers with only a few weeks of certainty. Haste here is expensive. A federal grant can leverage private credit, but it cannot compensate for a staple crop that never came up.

The shortage is no longer a purely rural problem. Towns that overlook how failed harvests are handled soon feel the pressure on prices. The incentive to recruit seasonal labour weakens once farms cannot pay. Some workers leave. Others stay and plant less.
Public money still arrives. What it rarely does is arrive before the decision to abandon a field has already been made. The tendency, unless the grant comes earlier, is to insure more and grow less.

quiz.q: A federal grant is described as
options: a full substitute for a lost harvest
a way to draw in private credit, not a replacement for the crop
the reason farmers plant more acreage
a payment that always arrives before sowing
quiz.why: but 把「撬动私人信贷」和「替代绝收」切开。A 是 but 前面的误读。

quiz.q: The author's main warning is that
options: seasonal workers prefer cities
aid often comes after farmers have already given up a field
droughts no longer affect prices
insurance has made farming risk-free
quiz.why: 末段 rarely 才是结论。D 把 insure more 夸成没有风险。

passages.title: The quiet hour
paragraphs: At a secondary school, the first week of a phone rule was unusually quiet. Students put their devices in sealed pouches before class. Compliance was high, and test scores rose slightly. The principal took this as proof that removing a screen could protect attention.

Yet a rule cannot teach the habit it replaces. Once pupils took their phones home, many returned to the same rapid stream of messages. A diligent student might put a device away without being told; another needs help deciding which alerts matter. Teachers also spent time trying to enforce the pouch rule when they had hoped to discuss how to judge information found online.

The school kept the pouches for exams but chose to scrap them during research projects. Now pupils explain when a device helps them learn and when it interrupts their thinking. The quiet hour was useful because it made that choice visible.

quiz.q: The author implies that the phone rule was most useful when it
options: raised every pupil's test score
prompted pupils to make deliberate choices about screen use
removed all technology from research projects
saved teachers time in every lesson
quiz.why: 末段强调让学生判断设备何时有助学习，禁令本身不是最终目标。

passages.title: The repair counter
paragraphs: When a household appliance fails, replacing it can seem cheaper than fixing it. The price tag, however, hides the cost of discarding a working motor because one small part has worn out. A local cooperative found that repair was often feasible, but only when customers could obtain parts and clear instructions.

The group opened a weekly counter where volunteers examine broken devices. They do not promise to save every machine. Some products are sealed so tightly that a repair would cost more than a new one. Yet the counter changes an earlier decision: people learn which products can be maintained before they buy them. A prominent repairability label can help, provided that it reflects real access to parts rather than a manufacturer's estimate.

To sustain the counter, local shops have agreed to keep common parts in stock. Its success should be measured by how many usable devices remain in homes, not by the crowd on opening day. The larger incentive lies with manufacturers: make a product that can be opened, and customers may retain it for longer.

quiz.q: A repairability label is useful only when it
options: promises that every machine can be saved
is written by the city rather than a manufacturer
reflects whether spare parts can actually be obtained
shows the lowest price of a replacement
quiz.why: 第二段的 provided that 限定了标签的价值：它必须反映零件能否实际买到。

quiz.q: The counter's success should be judged by
options: how many devices stay in use over time
the number of visitors on opening day
how quickly customers buy replacements
the amount of money spent on labels
quiz.why: 末段明确把仍在使用的设备数量作为标准，而非开业当天的人数。
